original.hypothesis: The bounded activity should stop. The immutable converged candidate (d=0.0) under target-based NMPC feedback with default tip-speed weights is already evaluated and is a valid_failure: sampled holding max position error 0.193 m and holding max speed 3.25 m/s (limits 0.01 m and 0.02 m/s) and terminal error 0.0955 m (limit 0.01 m). That failure is large and multiply confounded, with verifiable compute starvation (35/35 deadline misses, mean update 19.29 s vs the 0.01 s control period; 31/35 internal solves early-stopped on budget) and one-step model-plant disagreement up to 0.0094 m and 0.166 m/s. A single two-weight control-only revision addresses neither confound and so cannot act as a discriminating test; the two independent open-loop BDF replays already failed their disagreement gates. Therefore no remaining supported action can plausibly change the disposition, and no unique or dominant cause is established.
limitations: Closed-loop acceptance is sampled at 0.01 s with no continuous-time or real-time guarantee; it is not the dense 0.0005 s BDF criterion.
Exploratory simulated feedback only; no real hardware and no real-time deployment; 35/35 control deadline misses mean the NMPC was not executed in real time.
Multiple candidate causes (compute starvation, model-plant mismatch, control tuning, candidate structure) remain confounded; no unique or dominant cause is established.
Only the single candidate d=0.0 with default weights was evaluated under feedback; the two tip-speed weights were never varied in closed loop, so weight sensitivity is untested.
No design search, no weight sweep, and no alternative-structure evaluation were part of this step.
The evaluation reused the already-available immutable artifact; this decision added no new numerical work.
Results do not establish global optimality, physical impossibility, LLM superiority, or any old open-loop validation.
original.revision_or_stop_rule: STOP now with no further provider sends, backend launches, NLP solves or replays; seal all prior evidence as-is. Do not present the closed-loop failure as proving structural or physical impossibility, real-time infeasibility, or a unique/dominant error cause; do not present the failed open-loop replays as validating or invalidating the closed-loop evaluation; do not claim global optimality or that no design/weight could ever succeed.
original.weakening_observation: This STOP would be weakened by a supported action carrying a specific, falsifiable, non-confounded hypothesis that could plausibly flip the disposition — for example an isolated mechanism able to restore a feasible control rate or reduce model-plant mismatch enough to matter, or an isolated weight effect not already bounded by the observed 162-fold limit violation. No such mechanism has been demonstrated within the frozen specification.
